inputs.prompt: Keep exactly the same composition and camera: the first-person view sliding down inside this tube slide, the tube curving away ahead to a dark opening. Make it read unmistakably as a cheap children's play-place tube slide, not a spaceship or industrial pipe. Change the material and details only: one-piece rotomolded hollow plastic in a dull faded orange, thick and slightly wavy, with a soft matte chalky surface and no shine. The joints between sections are simple overlapping plastic collars held by a few round plastic bolt caps. No rivets, no metal rings, no steel bands, no panels, no machinery. No light fixtures inside the tube; the only light is a dim orange-brown glow coming through the translucent plastic walls from outside, brighter in faint patches. Less dirty than before: a well-used, rarely cleaned slide with dust in the bottom channel, scuffs and faint sock-and-shoe marks along the floor of the tube, a few faded sticker scraps, one small yellowed tape patch, sun-fading on the plastic. Gloomy and underlit, slightly murky, photographic 35mm film still, 1990s film grain. No hands, no people, no figures, no text, no logos.
